You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task note: task-87f587a7

## Hollow-square interiors colored by side-length parity (solved)

This task shows hollow square outlines (one-cell-thick borders) on a uniform background. Keep each outline and background unchanged; fill every cell strictly inside each square with a solid color determined by the square's outer side length:

- even side length -> color 2
- odd side length -> color 7

The interior is the square's bounding box inset by one cell on all sides. The rule applies separately to every outline, regardless of outline color or size. Do not infer fill from outline color; the demonstrated squares had several different outline colors and their interior fill followed only parity of outer side length.

### Evidence: demo pair
Input contained square outlines with side lengths 6 (color 6), 5 (color 4), 4 (color 1), and two side-length-3 squares (colors 1 and 6). The output preserved borders, filling the side-6 and side-4 interiors with 2, and side-5 and side-3 interiors with 7. Background remained unchanged.

### Accepted test
The 12x17 test had a 6x6 outline of color 9 (rows 5–10, columns 4–9 in 1-based coordinates), filled with 2 in its 4x4 interior, and a 5x5 outline of color 3 (rows 1–5, columns 11–15), filled with 7 in its 3x3 interior. All borders and background cells were preserved. Submitted output was accepted with 0 wrong attempts.

### Practical procedure
1. Locate each separate hollow square and measure its outer side length, including the border.
2. Preserve its one-cell border.
3. Fill its enclosed interior with 2 for even side length, or 7 for odd side length.
4. Leave all other cells as they were. Verify output dimensions and row widths.

## Additional evidence from the 2026-10-21 instance

Two more demonstrations and an accepted 16x29 test confirm the same parity rule, across varying border/background colors and square sizes. For the accepted test (1-based coordinates), the square frames were:

- color 6: rows 2–8, columns 1–7 (side 7, odd), interior filled with 7.
- color 1: rows 1–3, columns 20–22 (side 3, odd), interior filled with 7.
- color 1: rows 5–12, columns 11–18 (side 8, even), interior filled with 2.
- color 4: rows 5–9, columns 23–27 (side 5, odd), interior filled with 7.
- color 6: rows 11–13, columns 1–3 (side 3, odd), interior filled with 7.
- color 9: rows 12–14, columns 6–8 (side 3, odd), interior filled with 7.
- color 3: rows 11–14, columns 23–26 (side 4, even), interior filled with 2.

This instance was solved after one incorrect submission; the accepted fill distinguishes parity clearly: even-sized frames get 2; odd-sized frames get 7. The earlier failed attempt incorrectly used color 2 for several odd-side squares and altered the small ring center to 7 (which was coincidentally consistent with parity, but should be understood as filling its enclosed interior, not as a separate color-transform rule).
